message.content:
Explore the codebase at /bench/repo to understand its high-level structure. I need to know:
1. What kind of project this is (looks like a memo app with Go backend and React frontend)
2. The directory structure (top-level and key subdirectories)
3. Proto files location and service definitions
4. Database migration locations
5. Store layer structure
6. Frontend structure

Run these commands:
- ls -la /bench/repo/
- find /bench/repo -maxdepth 2 -type d | head -80
- find /bench/repo/proto -name "*.proto" | head -30
- find /bench/repo -path "*/migration/*" -o -path "*/migrations/*" | head -30
- ls /bench/repo/server/ if it exists, or find the Go server entry point
- ls /bench/repo/web/src/ if it exists

Be thorough and report all findings.

- codebase-memory: Use the codebase knowledge graph for structural code queries. Triggers on: explore the codebase, understand the architecture, what functions exist, show me the structure, who calls this function, what does X call, trace the call chain, find callers of, show dependencies, impact analysis, dead code, unused functions, high fan-out, refactor candidates, code quality audit, graph query syntax, Cypher query examples, edge types, how to use search_graph.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
Here are my findings:

---

## 1. Project Type

This is **Memos** (`github.com/usememos/memos`), an open-source memo/note-taking application with a **Go backend** and a **React 19 frontend**. The backend uses **Connect (ConnectRPC)** for its API layer (gRPC-compatible), and the frontend is built with **Vite** and uses **pnpm** as package manager. The frontend builds its release output directly into the server directory (`server/router/frontend/dist`), so the Go binary serves both the API and the SPA.

---

## 2. Directory Structure

**Top-level layout:**

| Directory/File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/` | Go entry point (`main.go`, `log.go`) |
| `/bench/repo/server/` | Server layer: HTTP server, auth, routing, CORS, notifications |
| `/bench/repo/internal/` | Internal Go packages (ai, email, filter, markdown, storage, webhook, etc.) |
| `/bench/repo/store/` | Data store / persistence layer |
| `/bench/repo/proto/` | Protobuf definitions and generated code |
| `/bench/repo/web/` | React frontend (Vite + pnpm) |
| `/bench/repo/scripts/` | Build/utility scripts |
| `/bench/repo/docs/` | Documentation and plans |
| `/bench/repo/.github/` | GitHub workflows and issue templates |

**Key `internal/` packages:** `ai`, `base`, `email`, `filter`, `httpgetter`, `idp`, `markdown`, `motionphoto`, `profile`, `scheduler`, `storage`, `testutil`, `util`, `version`, `webhook`

---

## 3. Proto Files and Service Definitions

**Proto files location:** `/bench/repo/proto/`

Three subdirectories:
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/` -- API service definitions (9 proto files)
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/` -- Storage/model protos (6 proto files)
- `/bench/repo/proto/gen/` -- Generated Go/TS code

**API Services defined (8 services):**

| Service | File | Key RPCs |
|---|---|---|
| **MemoService** | `memo_service.proto` | CreateMemo, ListMemos, GetMemo, UpdateMemo, DeleteMemo, SetMemoAttachments, ListMemoAttachments, SetMemoRelations, ListMemoRelations, CreateMemoComment, ListMemoComments, ListMemoReactions, UpsertMemoReaction, DeleteMemoReaction, CreateMemoShare, ListMemoShares, DeleteMemoShare, GetMemoByShare, GetLinkMetadata, BatchGetLinkMetadata |
| **UserService** | `user_service.proto` | ListUsers, BatchGetUsers, GetUser, CreateUser, UpdateUser, DeleteUser, ListAllUserStats, GetUserStats, GetUserSetting, UpdateUserSetting, ListUserSettings, ListLinkedIdentities |
| **AuthService** | `auth_service.proto` | GetCurrentUser, SignIn, SignOut, RefreshToken |
| **AttachmentService** | `attachment_service.proto` | CreateAttachment, ListAttachments, GetAttachment, UpdateAttachment, DeleteAttachment, BatchDeleteAttachments |
| **InstanceService** | `instance_service.proto` | GetInstanceProfile, GetInstanceSetting, BatchGetInstanceSettings, UpdateInstanceSetting, TestInstanceEmailSetting, GetInstanceStats |
| **IdentityProviderService** | `idp_service.proto` | ListIdentityProviders, GetIdentityProvider, CreateIdentityProvider, UpdateIdentityProvider, DeleteIdentityProvider |
| **ShortcutService** | `shortcut_service.proto` | ListShortcuts, GetShortcut, CreateShortcut, UpdateShortcut, DeleteShortcut |
| **AIService** | `ai_service.proto` | Transcribe |

**Store protos:** `memo.proto`, `attachment.proto`, `inbox.proto`, `idp.proto`, `instance_setting.proto`, `user_setting.proto`

---

## 4. Database Migrations

**Location:** `/bench/repo/store/migration/`

Three database backends are supported:
- `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/` -- versions 0.2 through 0.30, plus `LATEST.sql`
- `/bench/repo/store/migration/postgres/` -- versions 0.21 through 0.30, plus `LATEST.sql`
- `/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/` -- present but not listed in detail

Each version directory contains incremental migration SQL files. The migration orchestrator is at `/bench/repo/store/migrator.go`.

---

## 5. Store Layer Structure

**Location:** `/bench/repo/store/`

The store layer follows a clean pattern with a top-level interface/logic layer and per-database driver implementations:

**Top-level files (domain models and store interfaces):**
- `store.go` -- main store type
- `driver.go` -- database driver abstraction
- `memo.go`, `memo_relation.go`, `memo_share.go` -- memo persistence
- `user.go`, `user_delete.go`, `user_identity.go`, `user_setting.go` -- user persistence
- `attachment.go`, `reaction.go`, `inbox.go`, `idp.go` -- other entities
- `instance_setting.go`, `auth_config.go`, `deployment_config.go` -- config persistence
- `cache.go` + `cache/` -- caching layer
- `common.go` -- shared utilities
- `migrator.go` -- migration runner

**Database driver implementations** at `/bench/repo/store/db/`:
- `sqlite/` -- SQLite driver (17+ files mirroring the domain entities)
- `postgres/` -- PostgreSQL driver (16+ files)
- `mysql/` -- MySQL driver (17+ files)

Each driver directory has a main file (`sqlite.go`, `postgres.go`, `mysql.go`) plus per-entity query implementations (e.g., `memo.go`, `user.go`, `attachment.go`).

Additional subdirectories: `seed/` (demo data), `test/` (store tests).

---

## 6. Frontend Structure

**Location:** `/bench/repo/web/`

Built with **React 19**, **Vite**, **pnpm 11**, targeting Node >= 24.

**`/bench/repo/web/src/` layout:**

| Directory/File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `main.tsx` | App entry point |
| `App.tsx` | Root component |
| `index.css` | Global styles |
| `connect.ts` | ConnectRPC client setup |
| `auth-state.ts` | Auth state management |
| `i18n.ts` | Internationalization setup |
| `router/` | Route definitions |
| `pages/` | Page-level components (16 pages) |
| `components/` | Reusable components (60+ component files/directories) |
| `contexts/` | React contexts |
| `hooks/` | Custom hooks |
| `layouts/` | Layout components |
| `lib/` | Library utilities |
| `locales/` | i18n locale files |
| `themes/` | Theme definitions |
| `types/` | TypeScript type definitions |
| `utils/` | Utility functions |

**Pages:** Home, Explore, MemoDetail, UserProfile, SignIn, SignUp, AdminSignIn, AuthCallback, Setting, Inboxes, Attachments, Archived, Shortcuts, About, NotFound, PermissionDenied

**Key component groups:** MemoEditor, MemoView, MemoContent, MemoFilters, MemoExplorer, MemoPreview, MemoActionMenu, MemoCommentSection, MemoReactionListView, MemoDetailSidebar, MemoMetadata, PagedMemoList, AttachmentLibrary, Inbox, Settings, StatisticsView, TagTree, UserMemoMap, SearchBar, Navigation, and many more.

**Server routing** at `/bench/repo/server/router/` includes: `api/` (ConnectRPC service implementations), `fileserver/`, `frontend/` (SPA serving), `mcp/` (MCP protocol support), `rss/` (RSS feed). The SSE (Server-Sent Events) infrastructure is also in the API layer for real-time updates.
